clue.text: Military unit's club joined by army hero

definitions.note: the possessive 's here is read as 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay

parts.note: a bat is a club used in cricket or baseball
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
a lion is a brave person, a hero

explanation.surface: A regiment's sports club has been joined by a decorated soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: A battalion is a large body of infantry, a standard military formation.

clue.text: Workers' minder taking drink outside English stronghold

indicators.note: outside means the drink is placed around the other pieces

parts.note: beer is an alcoholic drink
a keep is the fortified central tower of a castle

explanation.surface: A factory supervisor drinks outside an English castle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Workers' are worker bees, not factory hands.
explanation.definitionFit: Worker bees are tended by an apiarist who looks after the hives.

clue.text: Soldiers who volunteer first in crisis, it's understood

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

indicators.note: first in points to the opening letter of the word crisis

parts.note: it, with the 's read as is linking to the definition

explanation.surface: In a crisis, volunteer soldiers are the first in, it is understood.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacit means implied without being spoken, as with a silent agreement.

clue.text: Obvious split after fathers go different ways

indicators.note: after places the word for split behind the two fathers
two fathers heading opposite ways means one is written backwards and the other forwards

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
pa again, the second of the two fathers
a rent is a split or tear

explanation.surface: A rift is plain once the fathers part company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go different ways' sends one PA backwards (AP) and leaves the other forwards, giving APPA.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparent means clearly visible or evident.

clue.text: Unskilled in employ receiving absolutely minimum wage

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so the wage goes inside the word for employ

parts.note: to exert strength is to employ it
P, a penny, the smallest possible payment

explanation.surface: Unskilled workers in employment are paid the bare minimum wage.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking skill or expertise means being clumsy and amateurish.

clue.text: New weapon of limited range

parts.note: an arrow is a weapon shot from a bow

explanation.surface: A new weapon has only a short range.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrow means restricted in breadth or scope.

clue.text: Took cover without hesitation, being warm and damp

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the word for took cover goes around the hesitation

parts.note: to hide is to take cover, past tense hid
um is the sound of a speaker's hesitation

explanation.surface: Someone ducked for cover at once, finding the place warm and damp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'with no', but here it means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Muggy, sticky weather is both warm and moist.

clue.text: Malicious trickster setting house on fire, right?

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above, so house sits on top of the word for fire

parts.note: to axe a worker is to fire them

explanation.surface: Is a spiteful prankster setting a house alight?
explanation.walkthrough: 'fire' looks like arson but means sack, and 'setting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoaxer deceives people with a hoax, a practical joke or fraud.

clue.text: Give me old-fashioned stuff, a thrilling play

indicators.note: fashioned means shaped or made, so the letters of old are formed anew

parts.note: to stuff is to cram or ram in

explanation.surface: Give me some old-fashioned stuff, an exciting stage drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old-fashioned' looks like one word, but 'fashioned' rearranges OLD into LOD; 'Give' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A melodrama is a sensational play with exaggerated characters and excitement.

clue.text: Discourage creatures crossing end of street

indicators.note: crossing means stretching across, so the creatures go around the letter

parts.note: deer are animals, creatures in a general sense

indicators.note: end of points to the last letter of the word street

explanation.surface: Discourage animals from crossing at the end of the road.
explanation.definitionFit: To deter is to put someone off doing something.

clue.text: Person on run varying paces with ease, we hear

indicators.note: varying tells us the letters of paces are changed into a new order
we hear signals that the word ease is to be taken by its sound

parts.note: ease said aloud is like E's, that is two letters E

explanation.surface: A runner keeps changing pace effortlessly, so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'varying' rearranges PACES into SCAPE; 'we hear' turns 'ease' into its sound, E's, two Es.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has broken out of prison is on the run, a fugitive.

clue.text: Again distribute old foreign coin collection

parts.note: the real was an old Spanish silver coin
a lot is a group of items sold together, a collection

explanation.surface: A dealer redistributes a collection of antique foreign coins.
explanation.definitionFit: To share out once more is to allot a second time.

clue.text: Husband leaves religious book in compound

indicators.note: leaves means goes away, so the husband's letter departs from the book's name

parts.note: Esther is a book of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A husband walks out, leaving his Bible behind in the commune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compound' looks like an enclosed settlement, but it is the chemical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: An ester is an organic chemical substance formed from an acid and an alcohol.

clue.text: One who is paid to sell animal feed?

parts.note: a pro, short for professional, is someone paid for what they do
a vender is one whose job is to sell, a variant spelling of vendor

explanation.surface: A salesman wonders whether he is paid to peddle fodder.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark warns that 'One who is paid to sell' is not a definition but a professional who sells, read as two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Provender is dry food such as hay or oats given to livestock.

clue.text: Hair-splitting editor brought in to criticise essay

definitions.note: an adjective in the clue standing for the noun, the practice of fussing over fine distinctions

indicators.note: brought in means placed inside, so the editor goes within the word for criticise

parts.note: to pan a show is to criticise it harshly
to essay is to attempt, to try

explanation.surface: A fussy editor is called in to tear apart a student's essay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essay' looks like a piece of writing but is the verb meaning attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive concern with trivial details and minor points is the mark of a pedant.

clue.text: Poet holds up train for girl coming out

indicators.note: holds means contains, so the poet goes around the turned word

parts.note: Dante is the Italian poet of the Divine Comedy

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word for train is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the Tube is the London Underground train

explanation.surface: A poet delays a train for a young woman getting off it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses TUBE to EBUT; a debutante 'comes out' into society.
explanation.definitionFit: A debutante is a young woman making her first appearance in society.

clue.text: Typical farm inmate

indicators.note: an inmate is one held inside, so the answer is lodged within the words typical farm

explanation.surface: A characteristic resident of a farmyard.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay: the young animal is lodged inside 'Typical farm'.
explanation.definitionFit: A young cow is one of the most common animals raised in a farmyard.

clue.text: Competition to get old writing implement for nothing

parts.note: something got for nothing is free
a style is an old name for a stylus used for writing

explanation.surface: A contest offers a free antique pen as a prize.
explanation.definitionFit: A freestyle is a swimming or skiing event in which competitors choose their own technique.

clue.text: Publicise policy right for a high-flier

parts.note: to air a view is to publicise it
a line is a policy, as in the party line

explanation.surface: Promoting the correct policy is right for an ambitious high achiever.
explanation.definitionFit: A passenger jet flies at great height, so it is literally a high-flier.

clue.text: Dwellings lacking restraint, initially, in the mews

indicators.note: placed in, just after the initial letter of the word for mews

parts.note: a mews is where hawks are kept caged, so cages
OTT, over the top, means excessive and lacking restraint

explanation.surface: Homes on a mews street with no restraints whatever.
explanation.walkthrough: A mews looks like a London backstreet, but its original sense is hawks' cages; OTT goes after the C.
explanation.definitionFit: Cottages are small houses, especially in the country.

clue.text: Polish youth leader's girl

parts.note: to rub something is to polish it

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here taken from youth

explanation.surface: A Polish youth leader has a girlfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' at the start of the clue looks like the nationality, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruby is a female first name.

clue.text: Navigation plan, going round island, takes time

indicators.note: going round means surrounding, so the plan wraps around the island

parts.note: a plot is a plan or scheme
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A sailing plan circling an island will take some time.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilotage is the act of steering a ship, especially through coastal waters.

clue.text: Main line? It's the bloody Tube!

definitions.meaning: an arterial route, a main road or railway line
a blood vessel, a tube carrying blood

explanation.surface: A commuter curses the Underground as the main line.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a major transport route and a vessel carrying blood from the heart.

clue.text: Service provided in the Peak District

parts.note: Mass is a church service
provided means if, as in provided that

explanation.surface: A church service is held in the Peak District, in Derbyshire.
explanation.walkthrough: The Peak District is a national park in Derbyshire, but here it means a mountainous district.
explanation.definitionFit: A massif is a compact group of mountains, a region of peaks.

clue.text: Current drop in force in Yorkshire, say

parts.note: a current is moving water
a fall is a drop

explanation.surface: Electric current drops sharply across Yorkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: In Yorkshire and the Lake District a waterfall is called a force, from Old Norse; 'say' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: In northern English dialect a force is a cascade, as in High Force in County Durham.

clue.text: Canon set up quarters in the country

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means the word is written from bottom to top

parts.note: a canon is a law or rule
E and S are compass points, quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: A clergyman sets up his lodgings out in the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canon' looks like a churchman but means law; 'set up' turns LAW into WAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Wales is one of the nations of the United Kingdom.

clue.text: Pianist finally copies cassettes

indicators.note: finally points to the very last letter of the word pianist

parts.note: to ape is to copy, so copies gives apes

explanation.surface: A pianist ends up copying cassettes.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassettes are reels of magnetic recording strip in a case.

clue.text: Courtyard a river engulfs not long after midnight

indicators.note: engulfs means swallows up, so the river wraps around the time

parts.note: the Po is the longest river in Italy
at one o'clock, written AT I with the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A river floods a courtyard soon after midnight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' is just a link; the time is AT I, at one o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: A patio is a paved outdoor area next to a house.

clue.text: Steps taken to identify cavalrymen

definitions.meaning: a nineteenth-century quadrille, a set of dance steps

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a square dance and a type of horse soldier.

clue.text: Description of errant type losing head regularly lately

indicators.note: losing head means the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a knight errant is a wandering knight, so his manner is described as knightly

explanation.surface: A portrait of a wayward character who has lately kept losing his head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'errant' suggests a wrongdoer, but it is the knight errant of romance.
explanation.definitionFit: Late in the day, every evening without fail, is the sense of each night.

clue.text: Like a germ that makes one ill?

definitions.meaning: germ in the sense of a seed, so like one is full of or like seeds

explanation.surface: Is a microbe something that makes a person sick?
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means both full of seeds and slightly unwell.

clue.text: Warning support is needed for part of the Strand

parts.note: fore is the golfer's shout warning of a ball in flight
a shore is a prop or support beam

explanation.surface: Warning: support is needed for a building on London's Strand.
explanation.walkthrough: The Strand is a famous London street, but a strand is also a beach.
explanation.definitionFit: A strand is a shoreline, and the foreshore is the stretch between high and low tide.
